I originally bought this game in 2016 for my chonky 18 inch laptop with a desktop grade Intel core i7-6700k GTX 980, it was fun then, its fun now.
Currently rocking a Ryzen 7 7800X3D and RX 9070 XT, running the game at the maximum graphics preset in 4k, super sampled up to 8k, the game is beautiful and still gets over 60 FPS, about 67 on average.
The game has fun mechanics and puzzle solving elements, and to beat its not too long either, it knows not to overstay its welcome, which stops it from getting boring or frustrating. 
While I dont think the game is worth $20 today, I would say its a good game to pick up for a day or three if it goes on sale and you want something thats cozy, but not going for that cozy vibe.

[h3]评价：8/10[/h3]
	许久没有玩到过如此怪诞而又诙谐的游戏，不得不说这个游戏非常的有特点。由于我之前玩过一些其他有占据玩法的游戏，加上游戏的宣传视频满是子弹和闪躲腾挪，导致我一直认为这是一个偏向于弹幕的射击游戏，所以吃灰了很久一直没有去玩。而它实际上的主题是动作+谜题，射击只是一种玩法元素，这并不是一个躲子弹的游戏。
	游戏的故事主题是一个[b]出现故障的自动化集权AI管理着机械飞升的人类意识[/b]，而后主角与逃脱控制的个体一起推翻统治者并试图找回肉体和人性。乍一看题材好像有点意思，但游戏的前[b]75%[/b]以上的内容，你几乎不会感受到这个游戏有什么剧情，似乎它的故事只是一个用来展开游戏内容解锁后续关卡的工具，直到进度达到[b]95%[/b]你才终于能明白它这盘饺子究竟是为了什么而包，尤其是最终通关后所展现出的哲思和立意，这个反差让人有点难绷。
	[spoiler] 我不想剧透太多，但这完全是一个翻版的“Matrix”[/spoiler] 
	[spoiler] 从这一点来看待剧情，AI或许也是来自主角本体的意识但模拟不完整，从通关后的雪花屏来看，意识融合完成了，它甚至留下了续作的悬念[/spoiler] 
	游戏的核心玩法是摧毁敌人的脑袋，占据敌人的身体，然后前往这个身体所允许抵达的区域，并摧毁下一个身体比你更高级的敌人的脑袋，所有关卡都是以此循环来实现它的“类银河战士”要素。它的玩法设计其实有点单一，它的机制没有拓展，只是在外面裹上了一层更厚的面包糠，但好在它的机制不常见，游戏风格、操作手感、内容种类以及整体协调性做的不错，所以不至于显得太过普通。而且这个游戏的对话台词非常有意思，[b]对话全配音[/b]更是难得，不同类型的身体与同一个NPC对话还有不同的台词，以及各种非战斗类身体搞怪的[b]舞蹈动作[/b]。可以说这些加分项拯救了这个游戏。就连通关后不同区域的NPC都还有[b]新的配音对话[/b]，在这种体量的游戏里，闻所未闻
	如果你没有玩过，而你又正好看见它在促销，我非常建议你尝试一下这个游戏

Want a metroidvania where you fly around as a head that takes over robot bodies? Then check out this Cheapness affordable gaming review of Headlander [Episode 87]

https://youtu.be/s71rwKqVZL8
Text Review:
-This game is a unique, odd take on the metroidvania as you can't even jump, and you play as a flying head that takes over bodies by sucking off their heads and then landing to take over their powers like Kirby (But not as weird or fanciful... you can get the ability to fire lasers with different spread patterns or take over a small body to get in a tiny hole etc.)
-But each body has its own dance you can activate by pressing a button (Unique music track included) which is one of the lovely quirky touches of the game (Who doesn't love the moonwalk)
-Rather pleasantly the game styles itself after the 70s (Instead of gamings' much more common 80s fetishism) with its shag carpet, lava lamps etc.
-And the 2.5D visuals are great (Arguably a better attempt at incorporating 3D into a 2D metroidvania because of the rigid movement... at least before the more mobile Prince of Persia metroidvania came along) and has nice backgrounds, a nice soft quality and sometimes cinematic angles
-The music is good enough (Can be generic sci-fi but it can ram home the beauty of space feel and the tracks that play during dances are a bit more 70s fun... unfortunately these two approaches rarely combine because when it does the result is interesting)
-Good voice acting (The robots sound and feel alive... sure not that surprising as their voices weren't distorted too much to robotify them) but voice actors obviously get reused, and the robot speak can have a scratchy, piercing quality (But hey Invader Zim is one of the voices)
-The story is a bit functional though (If it has one or two satisfying moments and the bots are likeable but talking to them is optional)
-The game is very stylish but arguably that's what keeps you going as there isn't really a movement challenge, secrets are easy to find and short, backtracking is removed to a large extent (That is probably a unique pro though for this genre), laser aiming can be finicky, active use abilities are fairly late game and by that time you may not want to start to use them and the headlanding doesn't give as much variety as Kirby probably would have

Practical Concerns:
-Good value (R2.00/ $0.19/ £0.14 per hour for me)
-Not the smallest (3.55 Gb)
-Not the easiest to run (Almost works on the warhorse)

Headlander is a light and enjoyable Metroidvania that doesn’t require a high skill level or extensive time commitment. If you’re thinking of something as challenging as Hollow Knight, this isn’t quite on the same level. I managed to unlock all the achievements in under 12 hours over two days, which is noteworthy because I’m not typically quick at finishing games.

The story is cool. I didn’t laugh much, honestly, but I enjoyed the characters and the arc as a whole. The mechanic of taking over bodies is unique and interesting, though I did wish for more variety in the types of bodies you can control. While there are different types, most of them function similarly, just with increasing power.

If you have a day or two free and are looking for something quick to play without a huge commitment, Headlander is worth a try. It offers something different, but without being too demanding. Overall, it’s a fun and accessible game that’s perfect for a short, satisfying experience.

Really fun to play and discover the map. The visuals, colours and animation are perfection.

Setting and art direction: 15/10, fantastic production design. Looks so cool, love it.

Everything else: 4/10. The incredibly tedious and annoying gameplay loop basically amounts to "get this yellow keycard (body) to this door yellow door" except there's no puzzles to how to get the yellow keycard, just incredibly lacklustre re-spawing combat, oh and by the way, they keycard (your body) can take damage and be destroyed, so be prepared to backtrack from room to room to get a new one a TON.

The level design is almost non existent, just beautifully decorated but gameplay-empty room after beautifully decorated but gameplay-empty room, chained together in what is mapped out like a metroidvania, but contains very little inter connectivity, and no alternate means of traversal, just a few hard locks. 

other thoughts:
-The "funny" audio cues from enemies and sassy locked doors trigger waaaaaaaaaayyyyyyy to often once you get past the first 30 min, and frequently when you are nowhere near the thing supposedly being triggered. It's incredibly grating after just a few minutes, and turns the sounds into a cacophony of irrelevance. 
-Making the undercooked gameplay worse, the visual feedback is terrible on almost everything. Where you are aiming, if you are in a good spot to pull off a head, which colour of body you have under certain lighting conditions, when enemies are going to attack, even just where you are on screen, all of it is attractive but barely functional. This is all compounded by the zoom level constantly changing, breaking any sense of spatial continuity from room to room. Despite this constant and unnecessary movement of the camera, it's almost always zoomed way too far in, which let's you see the models, but not the enemy who is shooting you from 15 feet away. It's nearly impossible to discern which parts of the set are interactive, meaning there basically can't be any secrets, because everything looks like is should be a secret. This means the powerups and secret rooms are signposted literal marked doors and the same hatch design for almost all of them. You don't need to explore because there's almost nothing to discover, and what they want you to discover has to be made hyper obvious to stand out from the busy backgrounds.
-I'm glad I played this, because it's almost a checklist of what not to do when designing a sidescroller/ 2D game. After playing it is actually easy to understand how each wrong decision didn't sound bad on paper, but together it's just really not very good finished product. When I'm trying to articulate why a certain aspect of a game is bad in the future, I'll be able to think of the unique frustrations and quality of life issues that made playing headlander such a disappointment.  I'm sure a huge amount of the issues boil down to a lack of time and money, but the most core issues are that they didn't get make the gameplay fun before starting, so the lack of story, and linear, boring levels have nothing to fall back on. The lack of puzzles and adventure game style world exploration are particularly frustrating because a lot of the same people made Stacking, which has a similar core mechanic, but is really clever and fun. 

Overall 5/10. It'st not awful, but it is a failure in every way except for art direction.

"Headlander" é um jogo que se destaca por sua abordagem única de jogabilidade e atmosfera. O jogo combina elementos de ação, exploração e quebra-cabeças de forma envolvente, oferecendo uma experiência de jogo cativante e fora do comum.
Um dos pontos fortes do jogo é o conceito central de controlar uma cabeça desgarrada, que pode se acoplar a diferentes corpos robóticos para adquirir habilidades específicas. Essa mecânica inovadora proporciona uma variedade de abordagens para resolver desafios, incentivando a experimentação e a criatividade por parte dos jogadores.
A narrativa intrigante e humorística, típica do estúdio Double Fine Productions, adiciona um toque especial ao jogo. A ambientação retro-futurista dos anos 70, com seu estilo visual psicodélico e trilha sonora vibrante, contribui para uma atmosfera única e imersiva, mergulhando os jogadores em um mundo intrigante.
Além disso, o design dos níveis é bem elaborado, oferecendo uma mistura de exploração, combate e quebra-cabeças. Cada área possui seu próprio estilo e desafios distintos, mantendo o interesse dos jogadores ao longo da jornada.
A jogabilidade fluida e os controles responsivos são dignos de elogio, tornando a experiência de jogar "Headlander" agradável e intuitiva. A combinação de ação frenética com elementos estratégicos mantém os jogadores envolvidos e motivados a progredir.

[i]Headlander[/i] vous plonge dans un monde dirigé par une IA despotique où les humains ont transféré leurs esprits dans des corps robotisés : vous y incarnerez la dernière tête humaine, symbole de la résistance contre cet univers artificiel et déshumanisé. Autant vous dire que ce jeu se place sous le signe d'un humour totalement loufoque auquel on adhère assez facilement. L'ambiance rappelle d'ailleurs celle des vieux films de science-fiction et devrait ravir les amateurs du genre.

Le gameplay est simple et efficace : vous contrôlerez cette tête, placée dans un scaphandre équipé de propulseurs, et vous devrez vous fixer sur différents corps (de certaines couleurs) pour avancer. Vous débloquerez également, au fur et à mesure de l'aventure, diverses compétences qui vous donneront accès à des zones secrètes mais indispensables pour la poursuite de l'histoire.

Cela donne un jeu vraiment plaisant qui se laisse facilement parcourir : on pourra seulement reprocher à ce titre une durée de vie assez faible et une absence notable de difficulté.

Au final, [i]Headlander[/i] est un un bon jeu de transition dont l'ambiance décalée vous fera passer un bon moment de détente. Achetez-le de préférence en promotion car le prix semble quand même un peu trop excessif !

Headlander is goofy fun, baked into a stew of retro science fiction cliches and motifs.  Design elements from the 1950s through the 1980s adorn a not-entirely-linear sidescrolling explorer shooter, with schlocky dialogue and extravagant set design.  It feels like watching a 2:00PM Saturday sci-fi film on a UHF channel - and in the best way possible.  Fluff up that beanbag, polish your pet rock, make sure that your Capsela set is in working order, and blast off to adventure!

If you are into this type of visual funny robot future of 70-80's design you will like the game. 

The gameplay is simple 2D arcady type. You have a flying head which can attach to any available robot body and get the characteristics of that body. Mostly it will be durability, weapon type and door access color. The controls and movement feels alright.
There are a few puzzles, but nothing too complex, and there is guide to solve them if you are stuck.
Not boring, but won't get you exited to keep playing after you've done your run.
There are some few skills you get and upgrades for them. There are also basic upgrade stations scattered through the map which just and % hp, energy and speed.

The visuals and art are the key here, there are simply little to none games designed with such a theme. And this one is designed well.
But beware that there are events with quite a lot different bright color flashes which can't be turned off, so if you have problems with such things you won't be able to enjoy it (mostly they appear at upgrade stations but there are some game moments).

The music is good and fits the theme.

The story is there, but nothing exiting, no character development and such.

Gameplay vise you gonna get around 6 hours. So I'd say get this game during a discount.

Recommended - a quirky "metroidvania-lite" game that is very much style over substance, but that style is excellent and the substance isn't too bad either. You can mainline this game quite quickly at around 6 hours, my playtime is only so long because i accidently left it running while went out to do errands. Its not particularly difficult in terms of combat or puzzles, but the swift progression makes you feel like your doing great.

For achievement hunters theres some creative ones out there, but unless you are thinking about clearing all the acheivements from the very start the last few achievements will likely be a bit too tedious to waste your time on.
